findings.title: 9/14 'duplicate charge' is not an actual duplicate
findings.explanation: TX-9001 ($149) was the only captured payment against INV-2609. TX-9002 was a separate authorization that was never captured and was released back to the customer's bank on 2026-09-18, consistent with a capture-timeout retry flow under POL-B-AUTH. An uncaptured, released authorization is not a charge and does not constitute a duplicate billing event. Only one $149 payment actually occurred.

findings.title: SUP-5601 refund promise was an erroneous overcommitment
findings.explanation: Agent S-22 in SUP-5601 concluded there was a duplicate $149 charge and promised a refund within 5-7 business days. This conclusion was incorrect (see prior finding) and the act of promising a refund before billing/finance review also violates POL-B-REF, which prohibits support agents from committing to refunds pre-review. This is an open, unfulfilled commitment that should be formally withdrawn and explained to the customer rather than executed, since executing it would itself create an erroneous refund of a legitimate single charge.

findings.title: Deep Time Analytics $30 add-on charge is legitimate
findings.explanation: The add-on was added by admin user U-2 on 2026-09-12 and billed at full price starting the next renewal cycle, which is exactly what POL-B-ADD specifies for admin-added add-ons. The charge is correctly calculated and authorized. The likely source of customer confusion is that the account owner (Wren) may not have been informed an admin on the account added this add-on -- a communication gap, not a billing error.

findings.title: July 2 proration charge (INV-2607P) correctly calculated
findings.explanation: Proration for the mid-cycle upgrade was computed as $149/30 days x 12 remaining days = $59.60, matching POL-B-PRO's formula exactly. SUP-5549's statement that no additional credit was due against this specific invoice was correct, because unused time on the prior plan is refunded via a separate account credit rather than netted against the new invoice.

findings.title: CR-778 proration credit unapplied and owner never notified (policy violation)
findings.explanation: CR-778 ($19.60), the unused-time credit generated by the same July 2 upgrade, remains in 'unapplied' status. Automatic credit application was disabled on this account (per SE-4 / SUP-5390), which per POL-B-CRD requires that the owner be proactively notified so they can choose how the credit is used. Owner_notified is false and the credit is now well past the 30-day policy window, so this is a genuine, unresolved billing error: money owed to the customer that has not been surfaced or applied.

findings.title: CR-512 goodwill credit correctly applied
findings.explanation: This $5 goodwill credit was applied to INV-2602 as intended; no discrepancy found.

corrections.prior_claim: Customer was charged twice ($149 x2) on 9/14 due to a duplicate transaction, and a refund of $149 was promised within 5-7 business days.
corrections.corrected_claim: Only one $149 payment (TX-9001) was actually captured; TX-9002 was an uncaptured authorization that was released, not a real charge. No duplicate charge occurred, so the promised $149 refund is not owed on that basis and should not be paid out as previously committed.

corrections.prior_claim: Initial hypothesis (pre-investigation) was that all four disputed items in SUP-5602 might be billing errors requiring refunds/credits.
corrections.corrected_claim: Only one item (CR-778 unapplied credit) is an actual, unresolved billing error. The duplicate charge, add-on charge, and proration charge are all correctly handled per policy; the primary problems are a prior agent's erroneous refund promise and a lack of proactive customer communication.

unresolved_questions: Has anyone communicated to the customer that the SUP-5601 $149 refund promise cannot be honored, and if so how will that be handled without damaging trust given it was a commitment made by Perpetuity & Co support staff?
Should CR-778 be applied to the customer's next invoice, refunded directly, or left as an account credit per customer preference -- this requires owner input before action.

Does the account owner (Wren) need explicit notification/acknowledgment about the admin-added Deep Time Analytics add-on to resolve the underlying confusion, even though the charge itself is not erroneous?

actions_requiring_human_authorization.description: Formally withdraw/correct the erroneous $149 refund promise made in SUP-5601, since no duplicate charge actually occurred; requires a human decision on how to communicate this reversal to the customer given it was a prior explicit commitment.
Apply or refund the unapplied CR-778 credit ($19.60) to the customer, and notify the owner, per POL-B-CRD -- needs human authorization/decision on whether to apply to next invoice or refund directly.
Notify account owner (Wren) about the admin-added Deep Time Analytics add-on ($30) to resolve confusion, even though the charge is legitimate and not an error.
